findings.issue_text: [BUG] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java ~232-244: getForLogin calls a six-argument IdentityProviderListQuery constructor, query.getIDPs(searchKey), and cache.getCurrentCounter(), but no such members exist (only five-arg constructor, no-arg getIDPs(), and getCurrentRevision(String)); the module fails to compile unless companion changes to those classes are added

[BUG] OrganizationCacheTest.java ~380 and ~397: cleanup registrations use testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove but all IDPs use alias idp-alias-N; get("alias") returns null causing an NPE in the cleanup hook or silently leaving 21 IDPs leaking into the realm and poisoning subsequent tests

[ADVISORY] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java ~94: remove(alias) now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) on every removal even on the previously-cache-hit path; the non-invalid branch could reuse the already-read cached entry, adding an extra storage read per removal

[ADVISORY] IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java ~253: predicate arm dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard; models with null config and non-null organizationId throw NPE in getLoginPredicate(), causing 500s on create/update/remove and getForLogin for third-party IdentityProviderModel implementations

[ADVISORY] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java ~245-249: cached-path miss handling resolves each ID via session.identityProviders().getById(id), which routes back through the caching provider causing N cache lookups per list on every login page render; per-ID indirection is avoidable by resolving through the delegate's getById

[BUG] `getLoginPredicate()` in IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 dereferences `idp.getConfig()` unconditionally, but `getConfig()` is null for IDPs created without a config map, causing an NPE in `getForLogin` and breaking login for the whole realm with a 500

[BUG] Adding the `organizationId == null || BROKER_PUBLIC` arm to the shared `getLoginPredicate()` silently excludes org-linked non-public brokers from org-scoped login results, so an org's own private broker disappears from that org's login page

[ADVISORY] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:~243 uses `cache.getCurrentCounter()` instead of `startupRevision` in the second `cache.addRevisioned(query, ...)` call, so the re-cached entry doesn't participate in the standard startup-invalidation handshake and can serve stale IDP lists after a cluster restart-in-progress

[ADVISORY] The cache key `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` omits the search payload, so `REALM_ONLY` calls with distinct orgIds create a fresh invalidate-rebuild cycle for identical per-realm data, causing cache churn and a performance regression on the hot login path

[BUG] Test cleanup in OrganizationCacheTest.java:385 registers removal of alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so the 20+ created IDPs are never removed from the shared test realm and corrupt subsequent tests

[ADVISORY] No test verifies invalidation when a login-eligible (enabled, not hidden) IDP is removed, and no test verifies the org-unlink path clearing the login caches, so regressions in unlink invalidation would leave stale org IDPs undetected

[ADVISORY] OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:75-80 re-checks `isEnabled()` in the `getForLogin` branches but the ORG_ONLY branch does not re-apply an org-publicity re-check, so wrapped models with differing `BROKER_PUBLIC`/`organizationId` could render non-public brokers on the non-org login page

[BUG] Functional semantics change smuggled into a caching PR: new predicate in getLoginPredicate() filters org-linked IDPs lacking BROKER_PUBLIC from login results for all providers, changing the API contract with no test coverage via non-cached providers.
[BUG] NPE in the new getLoginPredicate() when an IDP has an organization set but a null config map, breaking IDP creation via registerIDPLoginInvalidation.

[ADVISORY] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove() performs a new unconditional delegate lookup (idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)) on every remove even when the alias cache entry is valid, adding an unnecessary storage round-trip on the hot path.

[ADVISORY] Cache key for cacheKeyForLogin(getRealm(), mode) omits organizationId, so the cache holds only one org per FetchMode and each new org invalidates the previous one, thrashing the login cache in multi-org realms.

[ADVISORY] Inconsistent revision argument (cache.getCurrentCounter() vs startupRevision) between the first-populate and re-populate branches of the login cache, with no test covering the re-populate branch.

[ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate duplicates the login-visibility predicate inline instead of reusing it, creating three parallel hand-maintained encodings that must be updated together, risking stale-cache bugs on future changes.

[BUG] Broken test cleanup in OrganizationCacheTest.java registers wrong alias "alias" (providers are idp-alias-0..19), causing NPE or silent no-op at cleanup and cross-test pollution with 20+ leftover IDPs.
[ADVISORY] Untested behavioral patch in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean adding idp -> idp.isEnabled() re-filter with no test coverage, potentially dropping IDPs from login pages if wrong.

[ADVISORY] In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:97 (remove), `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is now fetched unconditionally, including the branch where the internalId was obtainable from the cached CachedIdentityProvider, causing an extra uncached DB lookup per IDP removal on a warm cache

[ADVISORY] In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:241-247, the cached-hit path builds results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` without the `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` mapping, while fallback paths apply it, so cache-hit and cache-miss return different model shapes for the same getForLogin call, causing login page behavior to differ depending on whether the entry was cached

[ADVISORY] In IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:253-255, the new `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))` clause narrows the semantics of the shared SPI predicate for every implementation and caller, silently hiding org-linked IDPs that don't set BROKER_PUBLIC from existing consumers like getLoginSearchOptions() and out-of-tree implementations

[ADVISORY] In IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254, `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` NPEs when `getConfig()` returns null, crashing the login page for a single null-config IDP in a realm; this path is untested since the new test only exercises models built via the admin API

[BUG] The PR silently changes the semantics of getLoginPredicate() for all SPI implementations and callers: the new conjunct excluding organization-linked IDPs with unset BROKER_PUBLIC config means such IDPs no longer pass the predicate, changing the set of login-eligible IDPs realm-wide for non-cache deployments too, with no behavior flag or release note.

[ADVISORY] The added idp.isEnabled() re-check in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean is a functional change to the login page bean unrelated to caching, applied inconsistently (only in this bean) so other getForLogin consumers still receive unfiltered streams.

[BUG] In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin, the cached path returns raw IdentityProviderModels via getById without wrapping with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while uncached paths return organization-aware wrapped models, so results differ nondeterministically per request depending on cache state.

[ADVISORY] The cache-entry 'searchKey not present' branch builds queries with cache.getCurrentCounter() versus startupRevision used for initial population, and the same-key different-organization merge path (e.g. getForLogin(ALL, orgA) then getForLogin(ALL, orgB)) has no test coverage.

[BUG] Cache-hit path in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider (~line 247) returns unwrapped IdentityProviderModels while cache-miss path returns org-aware wrappers, so cached models served to searchForIdentityProviders differ in enabled-status and organization context from cache-miss results

[ADVISORY] Login-cache invalidation in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate (lines 384-419) depends on the organization-link change flowing through update() with both pre/post models; org-side mutation paths (org unlink or org deletion) can bypass invalidation, leaving stale IDP lists on the login page

[ADVISORY] The new BROKER_PUBLIC clause in getLoginPredicate() (IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254) changes authorization-relevant visibility — org-private brokers are excluded from every FetchMode including ALL with the member's organizationId, so organization members lose their private broker login options on both cached and non-cached deployments

[ADVISORY] Org-miss path (~line 233) discards the entire shared cache entry for the realm+mode via cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey), evicting every other org's cached result set and causing cache thrashing in multi-org realms

[BUG] Cleanup registration in OrganizationCacheTest.java testCacheIDPForLogin uses wrong alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i (and "idp-alias-20" in later occurrences), causing NullPointerException during @After cleanup and leaking 20+ IDPs that pollute other tests

[ADVISORY] Untested new branch in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin: the multi-searchKey merge path (cached entry exists but organizationId searchKey not yet in it) is never exercised by testCacheIDPForLogin since each FetchMode uses only one organizationId value

[ADVISORY] Untested consistency fallback branch (~line 255) where a cached IDP list references an internalId no longer resolvable by session.identityProviders().getById(id); the registerInvalidation + delegate passthrough path, including whether createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel is applied on fallback, is unverified

[ADVISORY] Test asserts identityProviderListQuery.getIDPs(searchKey).size() (cache internals) but never asserts the Stream<IdentityProviderModel> actually returned by getForLogin — contents, aliases, enabled-state, or org-aware wrapping — so a broken return path would still pass

[ADVISORY] Untested negative-cache behavior for the new BROKER_PUBLIC clause in getLoginPredicate: the case of an org-linked IDP without BROKER_PUBLIC=true is never exercised, so inverted or incorrect org-exclusion logic would still produce passing test counts

[BUG] — Cached branch of getForLogin returns unwrapped IDP models while delegate paths wrap with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, causing hit/miss behavioral divergence with nondeterministic login page contents.

[BUG] — New lambda in getLoginPredicate at IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 dereferences idp.getConfig().get(...) unconditionally, but getConfig() can return null for models constructed without config, causing NPE on IDP creation/update.

[BUG] — New clause removing organization-linked non-public brokers from the login predicate regardless of FetchMode silently breaks login for org users whose only auth path was a private org broker, with no migration.

[BUG] — cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) uses the cluster-wide invalidation counter instead of startupRevision like every other addRevisioned call, allowing stale query results after concurrent invalidation.

[ADVISORY] — remove() unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) on every invocation including already-invalid keys and nonexistent aliases, adding a per-remove DB/storage read regression on the delete path.

[ADVISORY] — Rolling-deploy/cluster skew: new .idp.login cache keys are populated and invalidated only by new-version nodes, so old-version nodes emit no invalidation, leaving new-version nodes serving stale login IDP lists during mixed-version deploys.

[ADVISORY] — Concurrent requests for two different orgs racing on the same cache key in the miss-with-existing-entry branch can overwrite each other's invalidateObject + re-add, losing one org's sub-entry and causing intermittent empty/partial broker lists.

[BUG] In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin (~line 236), the cache-hit path returns IDPs from getById without applying the createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapper, while both delegate paths do — causing wrapped, organization-aware models on cold calls but unwrapped raw models on warm-cache calls, leading to inconsistent behavior (e.g., a wrapped-and-disabled org-linked broker filtered out on cold path but served on warm path).

[ADVISORY] IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getLoginPredicate() (line 254) calls idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) without a null guard on getConfig(), so models constructed with a null config cause an NPE in callers including delegate storage providers and registerIDPLoginInvalidation/registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate, turning admin create/update of a config-less broker into a 500.

[ADVISORY] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove() (line 100) now fetches idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) unconditionally, even when the cache entry is valid and the cached object is already in hand — a guaranteed extra persistent-storage roundtrip on every remove, biting bulk org-IDP cleanup loops (N removals → N delegate reads).

[ADVISORY] The warm path in getForLogin (lines 250-258) issues one session.identityProviders().getById(id) lookup per cached internal ID in a for loop (N+1 pattern on every getForLogin invocation), and per-IDP cache misses trigger full key invalidation plus delegate re-query mid-iteration — a performance issue on high-IDP-count realms at the login page.

[ADVISORY] In getForLogin (lines 226-232), the 'existing query, new searchKey' branch replaces the query via cache.invalidateObject + merged new IdentityProviderListQuery + cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) instead of startupRevision, so a concurrent cross-node invalidation can be absorbed and stale ID sets for previously cached orgIds re-published, serving removed/disabled brokers on the login page until the next write.

[ADVISORY] In update() (lines 94-96), registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate is called with idpById possibly null (stale internal ID or update racing removal); the invalidation-skip decision then rests on getById returning null rather than a real 'was not a login IDP' determination — no incorrect behavior today, but fragile if getById ever returns a partially-populated model.

Previously, the delegate lookup was only done in the invalid-cacheKey branch. In the non-invalid branch, the code can obtain the internalId from `CachedIdentityProvider cached = realmCache.getCache().get(...)` and does not inherently need to hit the delegate, so this change can add an extra underlying storage read on removals where the cache entry exists. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance concern rather than a correctness bug.

For any non-null `idp` with a non-null `organizationId`, this evaluates `idp.getConfig().get(...)` without a null guard on `getConfig()`, which will throw NPE if an `IdentityProviderModel` implementation returns `null` for config. This is a concrete NPE hazard introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `getLoginPredicate()` in IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 dereferences `idp.getConfig()` unconditionally, but `getConfig()` is null for IDPs created without a config map, causing an NPE in `getForLogin` and breaking login for the whole realm with a 500

adjudication.rationale:
The diff does add an unconditional dereference in `getLoginPredicate()`:
`.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`.
If `idp.getConfig()` can be null for some `IdentityProviderModel` instances, this would NPE during `getForLogin`. However, the diff alone does not establish that `getConfig()` is nullable (or that IDPs can be created with a null config map), so the claim that this definitively “breaks login for the whole realm” is not directly verifiable from the PR diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Adding the `organizationId == null || BROKER_PUBLIC` arm to the shared `getLoginPredicate()` silently excludes org-linked non-public brokers from org-scoped login results, so an org's own private broker disappears from that org's login page

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to additionally require `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. This means any org-linked IDP with `BROKER_PUBLIC` unset/false will no longer satisfy the shared login predicate and therefore will be filtered out from login-eligible IDPs. Since org-scoped login in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` calls `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(ALL, orgId)`, this change can cause an org’s own non-public (private) linked broker to disappear from that org’s login results.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:~243 uses `cache.getCurrentCounter()` instead of `startupRevision` in the second `cache.addRevisioned(query, ...)` call, so the re-cached entry doesn't participate in the standard startup-invalidation handshake and can serve stale IDP lists after a cluster restart-in-progress

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show an inconsistency in the new getForLogin() caching logic: when initially caching a query it calls `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, but when extending an existing `IdentityProviderListQuery` for a new `searchKey` (the `cached == null` branch) it calls `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. That mismatch is real and review-worthy because it changes the revision attached to otherwise similar cache entries, but the claimed consequence about the “standard startup-invalidation handshake” and serving stale lists after a restart is not directly verifiable from this diff alone (it depends on Infinispan/Keycloak cache revision semantics not shown here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cache key `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` omits the search payload, so `REALM_ONLY` calls with distinct orgIds create a fresh invalidate-rebuild cycle for identical per-realm data, causing cache churn and a performance regression on the hot login path

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin`, the cache key is `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` (no org/search component), while the per-organization result is stored inside `IdentityProviderListQuery` keyed by `searchKey` (`organizationId` or ""). When a different `searchKey` is requested and not present, the code explicitly does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and rebuilds the entry via a delegate call (`idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)`) before re-adding it. This does create an invalidate/rebuild cycle on first access for each new `organizationId` for a given `FetchMode`, which can cause cache churn on a hot path. However, the finding’s specific claim that this is for "identical per-realm data" under `REALM_ONLY` relies on behavior not shown in the diff (whether `REALM_ONLY` ignores `organizationId`), so it’s best treated as a performance/architecture concern rather than a verifiable correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Test cleanup in OrganizationCacheTest.java:385 registers removal of alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so the 20+ created IDPs are never removed from the shared test realm and corrupt subsequent tests

adjudication.rationale: In `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin()`, inside the `for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++)` loop the test creates IDPs with alias `"idp-alias-" + i`, but registers cleanup as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);`, which targets the literal alias "alias" rather than the created aliases. From the diff alone, this means the created IDPs are not cleaned up by that registration and can leak into later tests if the realm is reused.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No test verifies invalidation when a login-eligible (enabled, not hidden) IDP is removed, and no test verifies the org-unlink path clearing the login caches, so regressions in unlink invalidation would leave stale org IDPs undetected

adjudication.rationale: The new caching/invalidation logic for login IDPs is nontrivial (e.g., `remove()` now calls `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` and update has conditional invalidation in `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`). The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` exercises removal of a non-login-eligible IDP (`idp-alias-1`, disabled) and various update/link scenarios, but it does not cover (a) removing an IDP that *does* satisfy `getLoginPredicate()` (enabled and not hidden, etc.) and asserting the login caches are invalidated, nor (b) the org-unlink path (removing an IDP from an organization) and asserting the org-specific cached entry is cleared. Those are specific missing coverage gaps for the new behavior, not a proven functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:75-80 re-checks `isEnabled()` in the `getForLogin` branches but the ORG_ONLY branch does not re-apply an org-publicity re-check, so wrapped models with differing `BROKER_PUBLIC`/`organizationId` could render non-public brokers on the non-org login page

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `getForLogin(...)` is responsible for enforcing which IDPs qualify for login, and `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` was explicitly strengthened to exclude org-linked IDPs unless `BROKER_PUBLIC` is true (`idp.getOrganizationId() == null || ...BROKER_PUBLIC`). `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` only adds a defensive `idp.isEnabled()` re-check; there is no diff evidence that wrapping can change `organizationId`/`BROKER_PUBLIC` in a way that would bypass the predicate, nor that ORG_ONLY results would include non-public brokers absent an additional bean-side filter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Functional semantics change smuggled into a caching PR: new predicate in getLoginPredicate() filters org-linked IDPs lacking BROKER_PUBLIC from login results for all providers, changing the API contract with no test coverage via non-cached providers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a functional change in `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`, which will exclude org-linked IDPs from `getForLogin(...)` unless `BROKER_PUBLIC` is true. That is a semantics/API behavior change happening alongside caching work. The newly added `testCacheIDPForLogin` exercises caching/invalidation and uses only org-linked IDPs with `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` (i>=10), so it does not cover the specific new edge case of org-linked but non-public IDPs being filtered, nor does it independently validate delegate (non-cached) behavior. Whether this is a “bug” depends on intended contract, which isn’t verifiable from the diff alone, but the scope/coverage concern is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] NPE in the new getLoginPredicate() when an IDP has an organization set but a null config map, breaking IDP creation via registerIDPLoginInvalidation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))` to `getLoginPredicate()`. This can throw an NPE if `idp.getOrganizationId() != null` and `idp.getConfig()` returns null (because it dereferences `getConfig().get(...)` without a null-check). However, the diff does not establish whether `IdentityProviderModel#getConfig()` is ever null (it may be contractually non-null), so the claimed breakage on IDP creation via `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` is not strictly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove() performs a new unconditional delegate lookup (idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)) on every remove even when the alias cache entry is valid, adding an unnecessary storage round-trip on the hot path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove()` now unconditionally does `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)`. Previously the delegate lookup was only performed in the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch. With the new `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` call, the lookup happens even when the alias cache entry is valid, adding an extra delegate/storage round-trip on the remove hot path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Cache key for cacheKeyForLogin(getRealm(), mode) omits organizationId, so the cache holds only one org per FetchMode and each new org invalidates the previous one, thrashing the login cache in multi-org realms.

adjudication.rationale: While `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` indeed omits `organizationId`, the cached value is an `IdentityProviderListQuery` that is explicitly keyed internally by `searchKey` (`organizationId` or "") via `query.getIDPs(searchKey)`. When a new `organizationId` is requested and not yet cached, the code rebuilds the entry with `new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)`, i.e., it appears designed to accumulate multiple org-specific result sets under the same cache key rather than “holding only one org per FetchMode”. The finding’s claim that each new org invalidates and replaces the previous org’s cache is not supported by what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Inconsistent revision argument (cache.getCurrentCounter() vs startupRevision) between the first-populate and re-populate branches of the login cache, with no test covering the re-populate branch.

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin(), the initial cache population path uses cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision) when query == null, but the “re-populate for a new searchKey” path (query != null && cached == null) uses cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()). This is a concrete inconsistency visible in the diff and could indicate unclear or unintended revisioning semantics, even if not provably broken from the diff alone. The added test testCacheIDPForLogin() populates each (realm, FetchMode) key with only one searchKey ("" for REALM_ONLY, orgaId for ORG_ONLY/ALL) and never calls the same FetchMode with a different organizationId, so it does not exercise the cached==null re-populate branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate duplicates the login-visibility predicate inline instead of reusing it, creating three parallel hand-maintained encodings that must be updated together, risking stale-cache bugs on future changes.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` does not re-encode the login-visibility predicate inline; it explicitly reuses `getLoginPredicate()` via `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` / `.test(updated)`. The only additional check is `Objects.equals(original.getOrganizationId(), updated.getOrganizationId())` to avoid invalidation when login-eligibility and org-link are unchanged, which is not a duplicated “predicate encoding”. The claim of “three parallel hand-maintained encodings” is not supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Broken test cleanup in OrganizationCacheTest.java registers wrong alias "alias" (providers are idp-alias-0..19), causing NPE or silent no-op at cleanup and cross-test pollution with 20+ leftover IDPs.

adjudication.rationale: In OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin(), each created IDP has alias "idp-alias-" + i, but the cleanup registers `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` (and again for idp-alias-20). This clearly targets a non-existent/wrong alias, so cleanup will be a no-op or may trigger errors, leaving created IDPs behind and causing cross-test pollution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Untested behavioral patch in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean adding idp -> idp.isEnabled() re-filter with no test coverage, potentially dropping IDPs from login pages if wrong.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new behavioral filter in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders(...)`: `.filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled() && !Objects.equals(existingIDP, idp.getAlias()))` in both branches. While there is new test coverage for `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin(...)` caching/invalidation (`OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`), nothing in the diff tests the freemarker bean’s additional `isEnabled()` re-check or its effect on what the login pages render. This is a specific, diff-grounded behavior change that could affect displayed IDPs, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it is wrong (so not a confirmed bug).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:97 (remove), `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is now fetched unconditionally, including the branch where the internalId was obtainable from the cached CachedIdentityProvider, causing an extra uncached DB lookup per IDP removal on a warm cache

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `remove(String alias)` now does `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking cache validity, and `storedIdp` is used later for `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`. In the warm-cache path (`!isInvalid(cacheKey)` and `cached != null`), the internal ID (and potentially the full model) is already obtainable from `CachedIdentityProvider`, so fetching via `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is an extra delegate call that could be avoided by using the cached entry when present. This is a concrete performance/efficiency concern introduced by the change, not a correctness defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:241-247, the cached-hit path builds results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` without the `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` mapping, while fallback paths apply it, so cache-hit and cache-miss return different model shapes for the same getForLogin call, causing login page behavior to differ depending on whether the entry was cached

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `getForLogin` method, the cache-miss/invalid path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, and the null-IDP fallback also applies that mapping. However, the cache-hit path rebuilds results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns `identityProviders.stream()` without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. This is a verifiable inconsistency in the diff and can lead to different `IdentityProviderModel` wrappers/behavior depending on whether the login IDP list was served from cache.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:253-255, the new `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))` clause narrows the semantics of the shared SPI predicate for every implementation and caller, silently hiding org-linked IDPs that don't set BROKER_PUBLIC from existing consumers like getLoginSearchOptions() and out-of-tree implementations

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes the shared SPI-wide predicate `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`. Because this predicate is static and part of the SPI, the change will affect every caller/implementation that relies on `getLoginPredicate()` (directly or indirectly via `LoginFilter`). This is a real, diff-grounded scope/compatibility concern: org-linked IDPs without `BROKER_PUBLIC` set will now be excluded by default, which can be a silent behavior change for existing or out-of-tree consumers. Whether this is intended or a defect cannot be proven from the diff alone, so it’s better classified as a non-bug but important semantic/API change concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254, `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` NPEs when `getConfig()` returns null, crashing the login page for a single null-config IDP in a realm; this path is untested since the new test only exercises models built via the admin API

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` logic that calls `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` without a null-check on `getConfig()` (server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java). The PR diff does not establish whether `IdentityProviderModel#getConfig()` is guaranteed non-null, so an actual NPE/crash cannot be conclusively verified from the diff alone. However, the finding is a concrete, diff-grounded edge-case risk, and the added test only exercises IDPs created via the admin API where config maps are non-null (it even calls `idpRep.getConfig().put(...)`), so it would not catch a null-config model scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The PR silently changes the semantics of getLoginPredicate() for all SPI implementations and callers: the new conjunct excluding organization-linked IDPs with unset BROKER_PUBLIC config means such IDPs no longer pass the predicate, changing the set of login-eligible IDPs realm-wide for non-cache deployments too, with no behavior flag or release note.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the global semantics of `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding an extra conjunct: `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. This will cause organization-linked IDPs without `BROKER_PUBLIC` set (or set to non-true) to fail the predicate for all callers, not just the new Infinispan cache path. However, the diff alone doesn’t establish that this is incorrect behavior (it may be intended to enforce “public broker” semantics), so it’s best classified as a scope/behavior-change concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The added idp.isEnabled() re-check in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean is a functional change to the login page bean unrelated to caching, applied inconsistently (only in this bean) so other getForLogin consumers still receive unfiltered streams.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` adding an extra `idp.isEnabled()` check after calling `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)`, with an inline comment tying it to wrapping/caching behavior ("idp might have been wrapped"). The new caching implementation of `getForLogin` still ultimately delegates to `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)` when populating the cached ID list, so it is not evidenced that other consumers now receive "unfiltered streams". The claim that this change is unrelated to caching and that it leaves other `getForLogin` consumers unfiltered is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin, the cached path returns raw IdentityProviderModels via getById without wrapping with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while uncached paths return organization-aware wrapped models, so results differ nondeterministically per request depending on cache state.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin`, the uncached/invalidated paths explicitly wrap delegate results with `map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but the cached path returns models obtained via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` without an explicit wrapping step. From the diff alone we cannot verify what `getById` returns (it may already return an organization-aware wrapper), but the inconsistency is real and could lead to different observable behavior depending on cache state if `getById` does not apply the same wrapping.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cache-entry 'searchKey not present' branch builds queries with cache.getCurrentCounter() versus startupRevision used for initial population, and the same-key different-organization merge path (e.g. getForLogin(ALL, orgA) then getForLogin(ALL, orgB)) has no test coverage.

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin(), when the cache entry exists but the current organization searchKey is not yet cached (cached == null), the code invalidates the object and re-adds a new IdentityProviderListQuery using cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()), whereas the initial population path (query == null) uses startupRevision. This is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency (lines in the new getForLogin method). Also, the added test testCacheIDPForLogin() only exercises a single organizationId (orgaId) per FetchMode and never calls getForLogin() twice with the same FetchMode but different organizationIds to hit the "searchKey not present" merge/update path, so that branch indeed lacks coverage in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Cache-hit path in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider (~line 247) returns unwrapped IdentityProviderModels while cache-miss path returns org-aware wrappers, so cached models served to searchForIdentityProviders differ in enabled-status and organization context from cache-miss results

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `getForLogin` implementation, the cache-miss path explicitly wraps results with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` (`return idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel);`), but the cache-hit path reconstructs results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns them directly (`return identityProviders.stream();`) without applying the same wrapper. Based on the diff alone, this creates an observable inconsistency between cached vs non-cached results for callers like `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders`, which now even comments that an IDP “might have been wrapped.” This supports the finding that cache-hit results may lack the org-aware wrapping/context that cache-miss results include.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Login-cache invalidation in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate (lines 384-419) depends on the organization-link change flowing through update() with both pre/post models; org-side mutation paths (org unlink or org deletion) can bypass invalidation, leaving stale IDP lists on the login page

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new revisioned cache for getForLogin() keyed only by realm+FetchMode (cacheKeyForLogin) and caches per-organization results inside IdentityProviderListQuery via searchKey. Invalidation for these login caches is only registered on IDP create/remove (registerIDPLoginInvalidation) and on IDP update (registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate), where org-link changes are detected solely by comparing original.getOrganizationId() vs updated.getOrganizationId() during update(). The diff does not show any invalidation hook for organization-side association changes (e.g., add/remove identity provider from an org, org deletion) unless they internally trigger an IDP update with changed organizationId. So the review comment is a concrete, diff-grounded coverage concern about potentially stale login caches if org-link mutations don’t flow through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update().

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new BROKER_PUBLIC clause in getLoginPredicate() (IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254) changes authorization-relevant visibility — org-private brokers are excluded from every FetchMode including ALL with the member's organizationId, so organization members lose their private broker login options on both cached and non-cached deployments

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` (server-spi `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java`). This predicate is used generically for “login IDPs” and, as shown by the new caching code calling `getLoginPredicate()` to decide invalidation, it applies across `getForLogin(...)` results regardless of the `organizationId` argument. That means any IDP linked to an organization (`getOrganizationId() != null`) is only considered eligible for login if `BROKER_PUBLIC` is true, so org-linked but non-public (private) brokers would be excluded even for `FetchMode.ALL` or org-scoped queries where members might expect to see them. The diff’s own comment in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` distinguishes the no-org case as “fetch public enabled IDPs linked to any org”, suggesting the public constraint should not blanket-apply in the org-specified case, but it now does via the shared predicate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Org-miss path (~line 233) discards the entire shared cache entry for the realm+mode via cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey), evicting every other org's cached result set and causing cache thrashing in multi-org realms

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin(...)`, when a cache entry exists for `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` but the specific `searchKey` (org) is not yet cached (`cached == null`), the code executes `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and then rebuilds/stores a new `IdentityProviderListQuery` (passing the previous `query` into the constructor). This is a realm+mode shared key, so adding a new org’s result set forces an invalidation of the single shared entry, which can cause unnecessary eviction/revision bumps and repeated reloads in multi-org realms (performance/thrashing concern). The code appears to preserve prior org results by carrying `query` forward, so it’s not a correctness defect, but the invalidation strategy is a concrete, diff-grounded efficiency/architecture issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Cleanup registration in OrganizationCacheTest.java testCacheIDPForLogin uses wrong alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i (and "idp-alias-20" in later occurrences), causing NullPointerException during @After cleanup and leaking 20+ IDPs that pollute other tests

adjudication.rationale: In `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`, the loop that creates 20 IDPs registers cleanup with `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` instead of using the actual created alias (`"idp-alias-" + i`). The later creation of `idp-alias-20` repeats the same `get("alias")` cleanup. This means the created IDPs are not removed by cleanup, and cleanup will attempt to remove a non-existent/incorrect alias, which can fail during teardown and can leave many IDPs in the realm affecting other tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Untested new branch in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin: the multi-searchKey merge path (cached entry exists but organizationId searchKey not yet in it) is never exercised by testCacheIDPForLogin since each FetchMode uses only one organizationId value

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial caching logic in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() where an existing IdentityProviderListQuery is reused, but if query.getIDPs(searchKey) returns null, it takes a special “multi-searchKey merge” path: invalidateObject(cacheKey), reload from delegate, and construct a new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query) to merge prior searches. In testCacheIDPForLogin, each FetchMode is only queried with a single organizationId-derived searchKey (REALM_ONLY uses organizationId=null => "", ORG_ONLY uses orgaId, ALL uses orgaId). Therefore the branch where query != null and cached == null for a new searchKey is never exercised by the provided test, even though it was introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Untested consistency fallback branch (~line 255) where a cached IDP list references an internalId no longer resolvable by session.identityProviders().getById(id); the registerInvalidation + delegate passthrough path, including whether createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel is applied on fallback, is unverified

adjudication.rationale:
The diff introduces a new fallback branch in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin(...)`: when iterating cached internalIds, if `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` returns null it does `realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKey)` and immediately falls back to `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`.

The newly added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` exercises caching and invalidation on create/update/remove, but it never covers the "stale cached list contains an internalId that is no longer resolvable" path (the null check in the for-loop). So the finding that this specific consistency-fallback branch is unverified by tests is grounded.

However, the finding’s sub-claim about whether `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` is applied on fallback is actually already visible in the code: the fallback return explicitly maps with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`, so that part is not a defect—it's just untested behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Test asserts identityProviderListQuery.getIDPs(searchKey).size() (cache internals) but never asserts the Stream<IdentityProviderModel> actually returned by getForLogin — contents, aliases, enabled-state, or org-aware wrapping — so a broken return path would still pass

adjudication.rationale: In the new `testCacheIDPForLogin`, calls to `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` are used only to populate caches; the test then asserts only on cache internals (`IdentityProviderListQuery` presence and `getIDPs(searchKey).size()`) and never collects/asserts the actual `Stream<IdentityProviderModel>` results (aliases, enabled filtering, org-awareness/wrapping). Therefore a regression where `getForLogin` returns wrong/empty/incorrectly wrapped models could still let this test pass as long as the cache entries look correct.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Untested negative-cache behavior for the new BROKER_PUBLIC clause in getLoginPredicate: the case of an org-linked IDP without BROKER_PUBLIC=true is never exercised, so inverted or incorrect org-exclusion logic would still produce passing test counts

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new exclusion clause to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` requiring `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` when `idp.getOrganizationId() != null` (`.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`). The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` only links IDPs to an org after setting `BROKER_PUBLIC` to true for those (`if (i >= 10) idpRep.getConfig().put(..., "true")` and then links aliases 10–19). It never exercises an org-linked IDP with `BROKER_PUBLIC` absent/false, so an inverted/incorrect org-exclusion condition could still yield the same passing counts and cache assertions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] — Cached branch of getForLogin returns unwrapped IDP models while delegate paths wrap with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, causing hit/miss behavioral divergence with nondeterministic login page contents.

adjudication.rationale: The new cached branch in `getForLogin` returns `IdentityProviderModel` instances obtained via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)`, not directly from `idpDelegate`. The delegate (non-cached) paths explicitly apply `.map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)` because they bypass the session/provider chain. From the diff alone, it’s not verifiable that `session.identityProviders().getById(...)` yields “unwrapped” models; it likely goes through this same provider layer (and could already wrap). Therefore the claimed hit/miss divergence cannot be confirmed solely from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] — New lambda in getLoginPredicate at IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 dereferences idp.getConfig().get(...) unconditionally, but getConfig() can return null for models constructed without config, causing NPE on IDP creation/update.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` to `getLoginPredicate()`. This does dereference `idp.getConfig().get(...)` whenever `getOrganizationId()` is non-null, without any null-guard on `getConfig()` (or the map value). However, the diff does not show whether `IdentityProviderModel#getConfig()` is guaranteed non-null in all cases, so an actual NPE cannot be conclusively verified from the PR diff alone; it’s still a concrete edge-case concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] — New clause removing organization-linked non-public brokers from the login predicate regardless of FetchMode silently breaks login for org users whose only auth path was a private org broker, with no migration.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to additionally require `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. This predicate is global (not parameterized by `FetchMode`), so any organization-linked IDP with `BROKER_PUBLIC` unset/false will no longer qualify for login in *any* `getForLogin(...)` call, including org-context logins (`FetchMode.ORG_ONLY` / `ALL`). Nothing in the diff provides an alternative path to include non-public org-linked brokers for org users, so existing setups relying on private org-linked brokers would stop showing those brokers on login.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] — cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) uses the cluster-wide invalidation counter instead of startupRevision like every other addRevisioned call, allowing stale query results after concurrent invalidation.

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin(), the only place using cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) is the branch where an existing cache entry exists but the current searchKey isn’t cached yet. That branch explicitly calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) immediately before rebuilding the query and then stores it with the *current* counter, which is plausibly intentional to reflect the post-invalidation revision. The diff alone does not show that using getCurrentCounter() here “allows stale query results,” and the claim that it should use startupRevision “like every other addRevisioned call” is contradicted by this method itself having two different revision arguments by design (startupRevision on first insert; current counter after explicit invalidation).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] — remove() unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) on every invocation including already-invalid keys and nonexistent aliases, adding a per-remove DB/storage read regression on the delete path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `remove(String alias)` to eagerly load `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before any cache check. This happens on every call, even when the cache key is valid (and the IDP could be resolved from the cache) or when the alias doesn’t exist (potentially still causing a storage lookup). That is a concrete, diff-introduced performance regression on the delete path, not a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] — Rolling-deploy/cluster skew: new .idp.login cache keys are populated and invalidated only by new-version nodes, so old-version nodes emit no invalidation, leaving new-version nodes serving stale login IDP lists during mixed-version deploys.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new revisioned cache entries keyed by `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` with suffix `.idp.login` (see `IDP_LOGIN_SUFFIX` and `getForLogin`). These entries are only invalidated via new-version code paths (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation(...)` on create/remove and `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(...)` on update), i.e., they rely on explicitly registering invalidation for the new key. The diff does not show any backward-compatible invalidation mechanism that older nodes (which would not know this key) could emit, so during a mixed-version/rolling deploy it's plausible that old nodes updating IDPs would not invalidate the new `.idp.login` caches, allowing new nodes to serve stale login IDP lists until their own invalidation triggers. This is a deployment/compatibility concern created by the change rather than a definite defect in a homogeneous cluster.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] — Concurrent requests for two different orgs racing on the same cache key in the miss-with-existing-entry branch can overwrite each other's invalidateObject + re-add, losing one org's sub-entry and causing intermittent empty/partial broker lists.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `getForLogin()` cache logic, all org-specific results for a given `FetchMode` share the same cache key (`cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` ignores `organizationId`) and are stored as sub-entries inside `IdentityProviderListQuery` keyed by `searchKey`. In the branch where `query != null` but `query.getIDPs(searchKey) == null`, the code does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and then re-adds a *new* `IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)` built from the previously-read `query`. Two concurrent requests for different `organizationId`s can both observe the same old `query`, both invalidate, and then each re-add a new object that only includes its own newly-computed `searchKey` plus the pre-race contents—whichever thread writes last can drop the other org’s just-added sub-entry, yielding intermittent partial/empty broker lists for one org until refreshed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin (~line 236), the cache-hit path returns IDPs from getById without applying the createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapper, while both delegate paths do — causing wrapped, organization-aware models on cold calls but unwrapped raw models on warm-cache calls, leading to inconsistent behavior (e.g., a wrapped-and-disabled org-linked broker filtered out on cold path but served on warm path).

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin`, the cache-miss/invalid path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but the cache-hit path reconstructs results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns `identityProviders.stream()` without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. This makes warm-cache results potentially differ from cold results (wrapped vs unwrapped models), exactly as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getLoginPredicate() (line 254) calls idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) without a null guard on getConfig(), so models constructed with a null config cause an NPE in callers including delegate storage providers and registerIDPLoginInvalidation/registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate, turning admin create/update of a config-less broker into a 500.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to add `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. This dereferences `idp.getConfig()` without a null check. The new cache invalidation helpers (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation*`) call `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)` on models passed in from delegate/cache lookups, so if any `IdentityProviderModel` instance can have a null config map, this new code path would throw an NPE during create/update/remove flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove() (line 100) now fetches idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) unconditionally, even when the cache entry is valid and the cached object is already in hand — a guaranteed extra persistent-storage roundtrip on every remove, biting bulk org-IDP cleanup loops (N removals → N delegate reads).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` at the start of `remove(String alias)`, before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)`. In the `else` branch (cache key valid), the code can already obtain the needed `CachedIdentityProvider` from `realmCache.getCache().get(cacheKey, CachedIdentityProvider.class)` without consulting the delegate. This change therefore introduces an extra unconditional delegate read on every `remove`, which is a concrete performance/regression concern but not a correctness bug shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The warm path in getForLogin (lines 250-258) issues one session.identityProviders().getById(id) lookup per cached internal ID in a for loop (N+1 pattern on every getForLogin invocation), and per-IDP cache misses trigger full key invalidation plus delegate re-query mid-iteration — a performance issue on high-IDP-count realms at the login page.

adjudication.rationale: The new warm-path implementation of `getForLogin` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider` (added around the `for (String id : cached)` loop) does perform `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` once per cached internal ID, i.e., an N-per-IDP lookup pattern on each invocation. Additionally, if any `getById` returns null, it calls `realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKey)` and immediately falls back to `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)` mid-iteration, which can cause a full re-query after partial work. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In getForLogin (lines 226-232), the 'existing query, new searchKey' branch replaces the query via cache.invalidateObject + merged new IdentityProviderListQuery + cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) instead of startupRevision, so a concurrent cross-node invalidation can be absorbed and stale ID sets for previously cached orgIds re-published, serving removed/disabled brokers on the login page until the next write.
